verses.1: This is what the LORD says: The heavens are my throne, and the earth is the sole of my feet. Where is the house you will build for me, and where is the place of my rest?
verses.2: For all these things my hands have made, and all these things are mine, says the LORD. But to whom will I look? Not to the one who is arrogant and whose heart is proud, but to the one who is humble, who fears my word.
verses.3: The one who sacrifices a bull is as one who kills a man; the one who offers a lamb is as one who breaks a dog's neck. The one who presents a grain offering is as one who pours out pig's blood, and the one who burns incense is as one who blesses evil. These people have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations.
verses.4: But me, too, I will choose their inventions, and their hiding places I will bring upon them. For I have called and there is no one to answer, I have spoken and no one has listened. They have done evil in my sight, and they have chosen what I did not desire.
verses.5: Listen, all you who are trembling at my word, and let your brothers, the ones who hate you and despise you, say: "May the name of the LORD be glorified, and may it be revealed in your joy, and they will be put to shame."
verses.6: A voice of tumult from the city, a voice from the palace, a voice of the LORD who is repaying his enemies.
verses.7: Before the woman gave birth, before the pain came, she gave birth to a boy.
verses.8: Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen such things? For the earth to be born in one day, or for a nation to be born in a single moment? Yet Zion gave birth to her children in a single day.
verses.9: I said, "I will cause her to give birth," and did I cause her to give birth? says the LORD. Did I make her to be barren, or did I cause her to give birth? says your God.
verses.10: Rejoice for Jerusalem, and be glad for her, all you who love her. Be joyful with her, all you who mourn for her,
verses.11: that you may nurse and be satisfied from her breast of comfort, that you may be nourished and delighted from the abundance of her glory.
verses.12: For thus says the LORD: I will pour out peace upon her like a river, and the glory of the nations like a flowing stream. Her children will be carried on the shoulders and cradled on the knees.
verses.13: Just as a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you, and you will be comforted in Jerusalem.
verses.14: And you will see, and your heart will rejoice, and your bones will flourish like the grass. The hand of the LORD will be known to his servants, and his anger to his enemies.
verses.15: For behold, the LORD is coming with fire, and his chariots like a storm. To repay his anger and his burning wrath with a consuming fire.
verses.16: For the LORD will judge the whole earth with fire, and with his sword all flesh. Many will be the slain of the LORD.
verses.17: Those who purify themselves and cleanse themselves in the gardens, and who eat pig meat at the door, and who consume what is detestable and abominable—these will all be consumed together, says the LORD.
verses.18: But I will gather all nations and languages, and they will come and see my glory.
verses.19: I will set a sign among them, and I will send some of them as fugitives to the nations—Tarsis, Pul, and Lud, to Mosoch, Tubal, and Greece, to the distant islands where they have not heard my name or seen my glory. And they will declare my glory among the nations.
verses.20: And they will bring your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD, with horses and chariots, with mules and dromedaries, to my holy mountain, Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the sons of Israel bring their offerings to me in the house of the LORD.
verses.21: And from them I will take for myself priests and Levites, says the LORD.
verses.22: For just as the heavens and the earth I am making new will stand before me, says the LORD, so will your descendants and your name stand.
verses.23: And it will be that from new moon to new moon, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh will come to worship before me, says the LORD.
verses.24: And they will go out and see the corpses of the people who have transgressed against me. For their worm will not die, and their fire will not be quenched, and they will be a spectacle to all flesh.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "fears my word" — the Hebrew uses "chared" (fears) with "davar" (word), which is a poetic pairing.
- v. 9: "I will cause her to give birth" — the Hebrew is ambiguous about whether God is speaking of causing birth or not, depending on the context.
- v. 18: "I will set a sign among them" — the reference to "a sign" is to a divine mark or token, possibly a reference to the gospel or mission.
- v. 24: "their worm will not die" — poetic metaphor for the endless torment of the wicked.
raw:
[1] This is what the LORD says: The heavens are my throne, and the earth is the sole of my feet. Where is the house you will build for me, and where is the place of my rest?

[2] For all these things my hands have made, and all these things are mine, says the LORD. But to whom will I look? Not to the one who is arrogant and whose heart is proud, but to the one who is humble, who fears my word.

[3] The one who sacrifices a bull is as one who kills a man; the one who offers a lamb is as one who breaks a dog's neck. The one who presents a grain offering is as one who pours out pig's blood, and the one who burns incense is as one who blesses evil. These people have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations.

[4] But me, too, I will choose their inventions, and their hiding places I will bring upon them. For I have called and there is no one to answer, I have spoken and no one has listened. They have done evil in my sight, and they have chosen what I did not desire.

[5] Listen, all you who are trembling at my word, and let your brothers, the ones who hate you and despise you, say: "May the name of the LORD be glorified, and may it be revealed in your joy, and they will be put to shame."

[6] A voice of tumult from the city, a voice from the palace, a voice of the LORD who is repaying his enemies.

[7] Before the woman gave birth, before the pain came, she gave birth to a boy.

[8] Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen such things? For the earth to be born in one day, or for a nation to be born in a single moment? Yet Zion gave birth to her children in a single day.

[9] I said, "I will cause her to give birth," and did I cause her to give birth? says the LORD. Did I make her to be barren, or did I cause her to give birth? says your God.

[10] Rejoice for Jerusalem, and be glad for her, all you who love her. Be joyful with her, all you who mourn for her,

[11] that you may nurse and be satisfied from her breast of comfort, that you may be nourished and delighted from the abundance of her glory.

[12] For thus says the LORD: I will pour out peace upon her like a river, and the glory of the nations like a flowing stream. Her children will be carried on the shoulders and cradled on the knees.

[13] Just as a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you, and you will be comforted in Jerusalem.

[14] And you will see, and your heart will rejoice, and your bones will flourish like the grass. The hand of the LORD will be known to his servants, and his anger to his enemies.

[15] For behold, the LORD is coming with fire, and his chariots like a storm. To repay his anger and his burning wrath with a consuming fire.

[16] For the LORD will judge the whole earth with fire, and with his sword all flesh. Many will be the slain of the LORD.

[17] Those who purify themselves and cleanse themselves in the gardens, and who eat pig meat at the door, and who consume what is detestable and abominable—these will all be consumed together, says the LORD.

[18] But I will gather all nations and languages, and they will come and see my glory.

[19] I will set a sign among them, and I will send some of them as fugitives to the nations—Tarsis, Pul, and Lud, to Mosoch, Tubal, and Greece, to the distant islands where they have not heard my name or seen my glory. And they will declare my glory among the nations.

[20] And they will bring your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD, with horses and chariots, with mules and dromedaries, to my holy mountain, Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the sons of Israel bring their offerings to me in the house of the LORD.

[21] And from them I will take for myself priests and Levites, says the LORD.

[22] For just as the heavens and the earth I am making new will stand before me, says the LORD, so will your descendants and your name stand.

[23] And it will be that from new moon to new moon, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh will come to worship before me, says the LORD.

[24] And they will go out and see the corpses of the people who have transgressed against me. For their worm will not die, and their fire will not be quenched, and they will be a spectacle to all flesh.

Notes
- v. 2: "fears my word" — the Hebrew uses "chared" (fears) with "davar" (word), which is a poetic pairing.
- v. 9: "I will cause her to give birth" — the Hebrew is ambiguous about whether God is speaking of causing birth or not, depending on the context.
- v. 18: "I will set a sign among them" — the reference to "a sign" is to a divine mark or token, possibly a reference to the gospel or mission.
- v. 24: "their worm will not die" — poetic metaphor for the endless torment of the wicked.
